other_failure_modes.name: Improper categorical encoding
other_failure_modes.description: Categorical features are ordinal-encoded into arbitrary integers and treated as continuous numeric features across all models. The neural network scales them and passes them to a linear layer instead of using embeddings, and LightGBM/XGBoost are not informed of their categorical nature, forcing them to find arbitrary numerical splits.
other_failure_modes.evidence: tr_ord = np.array([cat_to_int[v] for v in tr_vals], dtype=np.int32) ... scaler.fit_transform(X_tr) ... nn_model = TabularNN(X_tr.shape[1])

other_failure_modes.name: Feature engineering leakage before splitting
other_failure_modes.description: Group-by aggregations on continuous features (e.g., mean/std grouped by a categorical column) are calculated over the entire training dataset before cross-validation splitting. This causes feature distributions from validation folds to leak into the training folds.
other_failure_modes.evidence: grouped = train_df.groupby(c_col)[num_col]; mean_map = grouped.mean().to_dict() ... computed before KFold

summary: The solution is generally well-structured, utilizing a robust 5-fold cross-validation scheme, out-of-fold target encoding, and a thoughtfully optimized ensemble of LightGBM, XGBoost, and a PyTorch Neural Network. However, it fails to handle categorical features correctly, treating arbitrary ordinal integers as continuous numerical values in both the tree models and the neural network. Additionally, there is minor feature-feature data leakage due to calculating group-by aggregations on the full training set before cross-validation splitting.
